scope_note: M2 'fit-input-2' batch: paired-fit (independent R vs Julia optimizations, n_init=1, se=FALSE) coverage of the 9 unbound `fit-input/` rows in docs/dev-log/core070/required-source-case-map.json (INPUT-ANIMAL-LATENT, INPUT-BINOMIAL-DEFAULT, INPUT-GAUSS-COMMON, INPUT-GAUSS-DEFAULT, INPUT-GAUSS-LOADINGS, INPUT-KERNEL-ONE, INPUT-KERNEL-TWO, INPUT-KERNEL-TWO-AUTO, INPUT-POISSON-DEFAULT). Only the NATIVE-MODEL / FORMULA-INTERFACE planned_case_ids from docs/dev-log/core070/family-required-case-plan.json are in scope; PUBLIC-R-BRIDGE case ids belong to a different agent's lane and are not covered here. Fresh small simulated fixtures are used throughout (n<=15 sites/units, p<=3 traits) rather than the pre-baked .rds artifacts in fit-input-subset.json, following tools/core070_namespace_2_batch.R's own convention -- the point is model-shape fidelity to each case's r_call, not byte-identical replay of a specific prepared dataset.

tolerances.justification: These cases compare INDEPENDENT optimizations (a fresh R gllvmTMB optim() run vs a fresh Julia Optim.LBFGS() run from each engine's own default start), not a same-point objective/gradient evaluation. The established paired-fit precedent in tests/testthat/test-julia-bridge.R (gllvmTMB lane) and tools/core070_namespace_2_batch.jl (this repo, 2026-09-01 calibration note) is 1e-4 absolute logLik/coef for independently-optimized paired fits; same-point identity checks elsewhere in core070 keep the tighter 1e-6..1e-8 band because those compare one shared theta, not two separate optimizer trajectories. 1e-4 is not a widening of any previously accepted contract for THIS batch -- it is this batch's first calibration, set to the already-established cross-batch precedent.

model_verification_note: Every EXECUTABLE_NOW row below was numerically spot-checked against a live frozen gllvmTMB 0.7.1 build (library at /private/tmp/structured-rho-library at authoring time) before this contract was frozen, at the exact fixture literals reproduced in tools/core070_fit_input_2_batch.R. Observed agreement at authoring time (single run, not the batch's own re-run): GAUSS-DEFAULT loglik delta 3.6e-9, GAUSS-LOADINGS loglik delta 2.1e-10, BINOMIAL-DEFAULT loglik delta 2.0e-11, ANIMAL-LATENT loglik delta 3.1e-9, KERNEL-ONE loglik delta 4.0e-8. This is why the frozen tolerance (1e-4) is far looser than the observed agreement: it protects against ordinary optimizer-seed/platform drift on re-run, not against a wrong-model mapping (which the authoring-time spot check already ruled out at ~1e-8 tightness).
critical_finding_kernel_two_auto: kernel_latent(..., unique = TRUE) requested on TWO OR MORE named tiers is silently reduced by gllvmTMB to the loadings-only (unique = FALSE) fit -- verified live: fitting INPUT-KERNEL-TWO's r_call with `unique = TRUE` added to both kernel_latent() terms reproduces the exact same logLik (-2.588663829612953, identical to 15 decimal places) and the same 3-coefficient parameter count as the plain two-kernel fit, on an authoring-time probe. This matches kernel-keywords.R's own docstring: 'Multi-kernel fits are loadings-only: unique = TRUE ... are not available in that combination' (.unlazy/core070-aghq/oracle-source/readback/R/kernel-keywords.R around the kernel_latent() roxygen block) -- gllvmTMB does not error on the combination, it drops the companion silently. INPUT-KERNEL-TWO-AUTO's Julia mapping therefore uses the SAME two-SourceCovariance call as INPUT-KERNEL-TWO (unique=false on both), NOT SourceCovariance(...; unique=true) -- using unique=true in Julia would fit a genuinely different (non-degenerate) model and silently become a wrong-model comparison, the exact defect class flagged in this task's brief.

cases.reason: gllvm(@formula(y ~ 1), Y, data; family = Normal(), K = 1) takes formula.jl's q==0 branch, which calls fit_gaussian_gllvm(Y; K=K) with NO X -- and fit_gaussian_gllvm's own convention is X=nothing means ZERO MEAN, not per-species intercepts. Verified live: this call gives logLik=-33.187092, not the R/native-Julia value -31.978555 (delta 1.21, far outside tolerance) on the authoring-time fixture. The only two @formula routes that DO give per-species intercepts are (a) pervar=true (which unconditionally adds a per-trait unique-variance block GAUSS-LOADINGS must NOT have) and (b) an explicit q>0 site-level covariate design (whose coefficients are shared ACROSS species by construction -- formula.jl:150-151 -- not per-species). formula.jl also explicitly forbids passing X directly alongside a formula ('Do not also supply X with a formula', formula.jl:150). There is no existing @formula front-door path that reproduces a per-species-intercept, loadings-only (no unique block), free-sigma_eps Gaussian model.
cases.evidence: src/formula.jl:196-201 (q==0 branch -> fit_gaussian_gllvm(Y;K=K,kwargs...), no X); src/fit.jl:66 (fit_gaussian_gllvm docstring: 'X=nothing means zero mean'); live probe at authoring time (/tmp/probe_formula.jl) reproduced the mismatch

cases.r_call: gllvmTMB(value ~ 0 + trait + latent(0 + trait | site, d = 1, common = TRUE), df, unit = 'site', trait = 'trait', family = gaussian(), control = gllvmTMBcontrol(n_init = 1L, se = FALSE))
cases.reason: common = TRUE ties the per-trait unique/diagonal variance to ONE shared scalar (fit-input-subset.json summary for INPUT-GAUSS-COMMON: free_theta_diag_B = 1, vs 3 for INPUT-GAUSS-DEFAULT). Neither of GLLVM.jl's two candidate surfaces supports a tied/shared diagonal-variance parameterisation: fit_gaussian_gllvm's has_diag block (src/fit.jl:90-124) is always per-trait (length p, one free sigma^2_B per trait, no tying option), and fit_gaussian_pervar_gllvm's ψ² (src/families/gaussian_pervar.jl:184-227) is likewise always per-trait. `grep -n "common" src/fit.jl src/families/gaussian_pervar.jl src/packing.jl` returns zero matches anywhere in the ordinary-latent-block code path. The only place a `common` flag exists in this codebase is SourceCovariance.common (src/source_fit.jl:1-46) in the UNRELATED fixed-source-kernel API (fit_gaussian_sources), which ties independent/unique SOURCE variances, not the ordinary latent() unique-diagonal block this row's r_call requests.
cases.evidence: src/fit.jl:66-124; src/families/gaussian_pervar.jl:184-227; src/source_fit.jl:1-46 (the only `common` flag in the repo, on the wrong API surface); grep -n "common" src/fit.jl src/families/gaussian_pervar.jl src/packing.jl -> no output

CRITICAL: R's default latent() Psi companion is auto-SKIPPED for single-trial binomial traits under gllvmTMB's own family-specific identifiability gate ('Skipping the default between-unit Psi for ... binary / categorical-contrast traits'; verified live, R reports npar=6 = 3 beta + 3 lambda, no unique block) -- so R's DEFAULT binomial model reduces to the SAME loadings-only shape fit_binomial_gllvm already implements. This is why BINOMIAL-DEFAULT is executable while POISSON-DEFAULT (whose default Psi is NOT auto-skipped) is not.
